title: Wire the Biblioteca and the reader to the library API
description:
## What changes for the user
This is the first moment Norte shows real saved links. After it lands, the Biblioteca lists what was actually saved, with the real counts in the sidebar, page by page; opening an item shows the article's extracted text in the reader, an "extraindo" state while that is still happening, and the reason plus a retry button when it failed. Marking read, moving to later or archive, and the place where reading stopped are kept by the server, and the Início save dialog saves for real.

## Outcome
The library module's frontend reads and writes the API instead of the mock: the Biblioteca view with its filters and cursor pagination, sidebar counts from the counts endpoint, the Material view rendering extracted HTML through a new `ArticleContent` component with pending polling and failed-retry states, read/status/position mutations, the open call on entry, the saved selection shown read-only, and the Início save dialog posting to the API. The library's mock slice is deleted.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `web/` is the Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript frontend; the Go server in `server/` serves it and the API from one binary, and `npm run dev` proxies `/api` to a running `norte serve`. Generated TypeScript types live in `web/src/api/<module>.d.ts`, and `web/src/api/client.ts` (openapi-fetch) is the one HTTP client.

Two earlier steps prepared this one. The frontend is organised into modules under `web/src/modules/<name>/`, each with a `manifest` declaring `backing: 'api' | 'mock'`; a module is mounted when it is `mock`, or `api` and listed by `GET /api/config`. Every store is a set of injected composables (`useLibraryItems`, `useLibraryItem(id)`) exposing `data`, `loading`, `error`, `refresh`, already returning the API's final shapes (`{items, next_cursor, counts}`, the detail record) from the mock, with mutations that update state only from the response. This bead is step three for the library: swap the composables' source to the API. The async data shape and the generic loading and error states should not need another migration; the view changes listed here (API wiring, pagination, reader states, the save dialog, `ArticleContent`) are this bead's own work, and only a further data-shape rewrite is reported as a defect of the previous step.

The library API this bead consumes: `GET /api/library/items` (`view=inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo`, `tipo`, `unread`, `sort`, `q`, `cursor`, `limit`; summaries only), `GET /api/library/counts` (`{views: {inbox, depois, arquivo, tudo}, kinds, unread}`), `GET /api/library/items/{id}` (full record including `content_html`, `extract_status` `pending|done|failed`, `extract_error`, `selection` `{exact, prefix, suffix}` or null, `read_position` `{v: 1, anchor, percent}`), `PATCH /api/library/items/{id}` (`status`, `unread`, `why`, `kind`, `title`, `read_position`), `POST /api/library/items/{id}/open`, `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract`, `POST /api/library/items`. Library status is `inbox|depois|arquivo` plus a separate `unread` flag and `read_at`.

Decided:

- **Swap the source.** The library composables call the API through `client.ts`; the library manifest becomes `backing: 'api'`; the library's mock slice is deleted, not kept as a fallback (the other modules' mock slices are self-contained and do not depend on it).
- **Biblioteca** (`LibraryView`): the existing filters (view, tipo, unread, sort) map to query parameters, and pagination is "carregar mais" over `next_cursor`. Sidebar counts come from `/api/library/counts`, refreshed after a mutation.
- **`ArticleContent`**, a new component, inserts the server's already-sanitized `content_html` with `v-html` (correct here because the server sanitized it with an allowlist; the component adds no sanitizer of its own) and, after every change of `content_html` (pending to final, or a re-extraction), waits for Vue's DOM update, removes the listeners it installed for the previous value, and walks the current anchors and images once to add what plain insertion cannot; unmount performs the same cleanup with one stylesheet covering every element the allowlist admits: headings, paragraphs, lists, blockquote, pre/code, em/strong, links, images, figure/figcaption, tables, hr. External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Images load lazily (`loading="lazy"`) and an image that fails to load is replaced by its `alt` text (an `error` listener added in that walk). Images are fetched from their source host by the browser; that is accepted and documented in a comment (a proxy only if privacy or availability makes it necessary). It replaces `MaterialReader`'s hand-written Vue nodes for articles.
- **Reader states.** While `extract_status = pending`, the reader shows "extraindo" and polls the detail with backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, then every 10 s, stopping on leave). When `failed`, it shows `extract_error` and a retry button calling `POST …/extract`.
- **Reader route.** The API-backed reader is `/biblioteca/:id` (the item's UUID); the old `/material/:kind/:id` stays for mock-backed study materials. This is the path the server puts in Telegram replies and in search entries.
- **Reading actions.** Mark read/unread (`PATCH unread`), status changes, `read_position` saved on scroll (debounced, 2 s) as `{v: 1, anchor, percent}`, where `anchor` is the `anchor` of the `content_headings` entry nearest above the viewport (the element with that `id` in the rendered article) and `percent` the scroll fraction; on opening, after the final HTML is mounted, the reader restores a saved anchor that still exists, otherwise the saved percent clamped to [0, 1], and writes no position while restoring; `POST …/open` on entry. The selection captured at save time, when present, is shown read-only as "trecho selecionado ao salvar"; turning it into a highlight arrives with the notes work.
- **Início save dialog** (`HomeView`'s dialog, `saveLink`) posts `{url, why?}` to `POST /api/library/items` and shows the new item; today it calls a mock `addSavedLink` that always sets `kind: 'post'`, `status: 'inbox'` and a fixed date.
- **Cross-module actions** from a library item toward study or projects stay hidden while those are mock-backed (the gating rule: target mounted and same `backing`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With `norte serve` running and an item saved by `norte save <fixture>`, the Biblioteca shows it, the sidebar counts match `/api/library/counts`, and the reader shows its extracted text — with the library's mock slice deleted from the tree.
- [ ] A component test with a fake API returning `extract_status: pending` then `done` shows "extraindo" and then the article, and stops polling on unmount.
- [ ] With `extract_status: failed`, the reader shows `extract_error` and the retry button issues `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract`.
- [ ] An `ArticleContent` fixture test renders each allowlisted element and asserts external links carry `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and images carry `loading="lazy"`; dispatching an `error` event on an image makes its `alt` text visible in its place.
- [ ] A component that changes from pending to final HTML decorates the final links and images; replacing the HTML again leaves one error listener per current image and none on removed nodes.
- [ ] Reopening an item scrolls to its saved heading anchor; after a re-extraction that removed that heading, it falls back to the saved percent; restoring issues no `PATCH`.
- [ ] Scrolling the reader issues at most one `PATCH read_position` per 2 s; opening an item issues one `POST …/open`.
- [ ] A saved selection is shown under "trecho selecionado ao salvar"; an item without one shows nothing there.
- [ ] Loading 120 items shows 50, then 100, then 120 via "carregar mais", with no duplicates.
- [ ] The Início save dialog creates an item through the API and it appears in the Biblioteca without a reload.
- [ ] `npm test` and `bin/ci` pass.
- [ ] Done when: a link saved by `norte save` is readable in the browser with no mock data involved, and a failed extraction shows its error and can be retried from the UI.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + `@vue/test-utils`, jsdom, a fake API provider): Biblioteca filters and pagination; reader pending/done/failed; retry; debounced position; open call; save dialog.
- Fixture (Vitest): `ArticleContent` over a fixture HTML containing every allowlisted element.
- Manual check recorded in the PR: one real saved article read in the browser against `norte serve`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/modules/library/` (composables' source, Biblioteca and Material views, new `ArticleContent` component, deletion of the mock slice), `web/src/shell/` (Início save dialog, sidebar counts).
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/client.ts`, `web/src/api/library.d.ts`, `bin/ci` (run as the gate, not edited), the server (run, not edited).

Frontend only, the library module and the shell. Size L: the source swap, the views, the new component, their tests and the mock-slice deletion exceed five edited files.

title: Match the Início screen to its prototype
description:
## What changes for the user
On the Início screen today there is no search field in the top bar, the curricula under "Continuar estudando" show a dash where a "Continuar" button should be and no percentage, the reading cards under "Continuar lendo" give no sense of how far each item has been read or where it comes from, and the saved items show raw dates like `2026-10-01`. After this lands the screen looks and reads like the prototype: search sits next to "Salvar link", each curriculum shows its progress and a "Continuar" button, each reading card shows its progress bar and source site, and saved items say "hoje", "ontem" or "29 set".

## Outcome
The `/` route matches the prototype "Norte - Command Home (standalone).html" at 1440px in both themes, region by region, apart from the invented mock text: top-bar search field, curriculum rows with percent and "Continuar" button, reading cards with progress bar and domain line, saved rows with relative dates and full meta line.

## Context
Norte is a Vue 3 frontend (under `web/`) ported from a design-tool prototype; every screen runs on mock data in `web/src/mock/`. The Início screen (`web/src/views/HomeView.vue`) was built from a bead whose acceptance included a 1440px side-by-side check that was never run, because no headless browser was reachable for that worker. A visual comparison run afterwards with headless Chromium at 1440x900, both themes, found these differences against the prototype (text content differs on purpose and is not a defect):

1. Top bar: the prototype has a search input with placeholder "Buscar artigos, notas, cursos…" to the left of "Salvar link"; the app has none.
2. "Continuar estudando" rows: the prototype shows, per row, the title; a subtitle line "<module> · <lesson>" followed by a mono `item x/y`; on the right a progress bar with the percent in mono underneath (e.g. `38%`), and an outlined "Continuar" button that routes to the curriculum. The app shows a "–" in place of the button, no percent, and `item x/y` stacked to the right of the bar.
3. "Continuar lendo" cards: the prototype draws a thin accent progress bar along the bottom edge of the cover placeholder, sized to the read fraction, then a mono domain line (e.g. `gwern.net`), the title, and "<author> · <N> min restantes" with the minutes in mono. The app has no progress bar and no domain line, and its meta line is "<Kind> · N min restantes".
4. "Salvos recentemente" rows: the prototype's meta line is "<domain> · <author> · <N> min · <kind>" with the minutes in mono, and the right-hand date is relative in mono: "hoje" for today, "ontem" for yesterday, otherwise day plus lowercase three-letter Portuguese month ("29 set"). The app shows "<author> · <kind>" and an ISO date.

Where the markup, spacing and type for each region live: `/home/gabriel/repositories/norte/design/prototypes/Command_Home/template.html` (the prototype directory is git-ignored and exists only in the main checkout; read it there, read-only). The repo is public: never copy the prototype's mock text; extend the neutral invented mock data with the fields these regions need (domain, read progress, lesson, minutes, saved date) when it lacks them. UI strings are Portuguese.

The search input only needs to render and accept text here; wiring it to a search backend is out of scope (there is no backend).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The Início top bar renders a text input with placeholder "Buscar artigos, notas, cursos…" left of "Salvar link", as in the prototype.
- [ ] Each "Continuar estudando" row shows title, "<module> · <lesson> · item x/y", a progress bar with the integer percent in mono below it, and an outlined "Continuar" button routing to `/curriculos/:slug`; no "–" placeholder remains.
- [ ] Each "Continuar lendo" card shows an accent progress bar on the bottom edge of its cover, width equal to the item's read fraction, a mono domain line, the title, and "<author> · <N> min restantes".
- [ ] Each "Salvos recentemente" row shows "<domain> · <author> · <N> min · <kind>" and a mono relative date: "hoje", "ontem", or "<day> <mmm>" with the month as `jan fev mar abr mai jun jul ago set out nov dez`.
- [ ] A 1440x900 screenshot of `/` next to one of the prototype standalone export, in light and dark, shows the same regions, order and alignment (text content excepted); the comparison is run with Playwright headless Chromium from a throwaway script outside the repo, and Playwright is not added as a dependency.
- [ ] Done when: the four regions above match the prototype and `cd web && npm run build && npm test` passes.

## Tests
- Unit: the relative-date formatter returns "hoje", "ontem" and "29 set" for today, yesterday and an older date, given a fixed "now".
- Component (Vitest + @vue/test-utils, real router and mock data): HomeView renders the search input, a "Continuar" button per curriculum row that routes to its curriculum, the percent text, a progress element per reading card, and relative dates in the saved list.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/views/HomeView.vue`, `web/src/views/HomeView.test.ts`, `web/src/mock/types.ts`, `web/src/mock/library.ts`, `web/src/mock/learning.ts`
**Reads only:** `design/prototypes/Command_Home/template.html`, `web/src/components/ds/`

Confined to the Início view and the mock fields it reads; the sidebar, the shell and the shared design-system components are not changed (if a ds component cannot show a needed element, compose it inside HomeView instead).

Saved reading has nowhere to live today. After this lands, you can see the inbox, push items to later, archive them, mark them read and filter by type.

The Biblioteca list with views, type filter, sort, unread filter and per-item actions.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.

Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.

- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

title: Reorganise the frontend into modules mounted by /api/config
description:
## What changes for the user
Today every part of the app is always there, the app promises offline use and sync it does not have, and nothing reacts to whether the server is running. After this lands, the app asks the server which products are switched on before it opens: a product that is off disappears from the sidebar and the home, its address shows a plain "módulo desligado" page instead of a broken screen, and when the server is not answering the app says "servidor indisponível" and retries by itself. The sidebar line "Sincronizado há 2 min" and the preferences text about sync, which describe something that does not exist, are gone.

## Outcome
`web/src` is reorganised into one folder per module plus a shell. Each module exports its routes, sidebar entries, home blocks, search entries and a static manifest declaring whether it is backed by the mock or by the API. The app fetches `GET /api/config` before mounting and mounts each module by one rule. Cross-module actions are gated by one rule. The retired offline and sync copy is rewritten and a test keeps it out.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `web/` is its Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript frontend; today every data-backed product view reads one `reactive` singleton, `store`, from `web/src/mock/store.ts` (created at line 236, seeded from `web/src/mock/data.ts`), and the views that change data call its methods synchronously; the placeholder view and the design-system gallery do not use it. The backend is a Go server that already answers `GET /api/config` with `{modules: [...], version, llm, telegram, timezone}` — the list of modules switched on by its `NORTE_MODULES` setting — and generates TypeScript types into `web/src/api/`, with `web/src/api/client.ts` as the one HTTP client.

The server-side products are modules: `library` (reading), `notes` (highlights, annotations, questions — written into by both reading and study), `study`, `review` and `projects`. Only library and notes get a backend in this first delivery; study, review and projects stay on mock data for weeks. This bead is the first of three steps that replace the mock seam without breaking the app at any point: (1) reorganise into modules — this bead; (2) make every store asynchronous over the mock; (3) swap each module's data source to the API, slice by slice.

Today's layout: views in `web/src/views/` (14 files: Area, Curriculum, Decision, DsGallery, Home, Library, Material, Notes, Placeholder, Project, Projects, Review, StudyHome, Task, plus sub-components under `CurriculumView/`, `MaterialView/`, `ProjectView/`, `TaskView/`), mock data in `web/src/mock/` (`data.ts`, `learning.ts`, `library.ts`, `life.ts`, `notes.ts`, `study.ts`, `types.ts`, `store.ts`), the router in `web/src/router/index.ts` (routes at lines 28-73), the shell in `web/src/components/AppShell.vue`, `AppSidebar.vue`, `ShellOverlay.vue` (the command palette and the preferences dialog), the search index in `web/src/search/index.ts`, the design system in `web/src/components/ds/` (stays where it is). 37 Vitest files sit next to their sources.

What this bead does, decided:

- **Move into modules.** `web/src/modules/<name>/` for `library`, `notes`, `study`, `review`, `projects`, each holding its views, components, mock slice and an `index.ts`; `web/src/shell/` for the sidebar, home, command palette and preferences; the design-system gallery `DsGallery.vue` moves to `web/src/components/ds/gallery/` and `Placeholder.vue` to `web/src/shell/`, so `web/src/views/` is deleted. Each `index.ts` exports `routes`, `sidebar`, `homeBlocks`, `searchEntries` and a static `manifest` (`name`, `backing: 'api' | 'mock'`, route paths) the shell can read without mounting the module. Routes are lazy (`() => import(...)`).
- **Config before mount.** `main.ts` fetches `GET /api/config` before mounting the app; while it fails, it shows a "servidor indisponível" screen that retries (every 2 s, then backing off to 10 s).
- **The mount rule.** A module is mounted when its `backing` is `mock`, or when it is `api` and `/api/config` lists it. So in this delivery the mock-backed study, review and projects screens keep working while the library follows the server. For a path in a module's manifest that is not mounted, the router shows a "módulo desligado" page. The sidebar and the home show only mounted modules. One cross-module presentation rule carries over from today's app: when both `study` and `review` are mounted, Revisão is nested under Estudo; when `review` is mounted without `study`, Revisão is its own top-level entry.
- **The gating rule for cross-module actions** (link to a curriculum, make a task, add as material): offered only when the target module is mounted **and** its `backing` equals the source item's. Real ids are UUIDs, mock ids are strings like `saved-link-3`, and nothing may join the two: an `api` item never points at `mock` data and a `mock` item never points at the server. Core entities (subjects, links, focus, search) are not a module; each one becomes API-backed when its endpoint lands (subjects and focus with the subjects bead, search with the home-and-search bead). At the end of this bead only `/api/config` and `/api/health` exist, so the existing mock subject and search data stay behind mock providers until then. The gating rule above is about module-owned entities only.
- **Self-contained mock slices.** The mock study, review and notes data that reference library items today (`libraryItemId`, `sourceLibraryItemId`, `materialId`) get their own small set of mock items inside their slice, so deleting the library's mock slice later breaks nothing.
- **Mock data still backs everything** at the end of this bead; every module's manifest says `mock` except where a test sets `api`.
- **Retired copy.** The app is a client-server app: without the server nothing loads. The copy that makes unsupported sync claims is rewritten: the sidebar line "Sincronizado há {{ store.syncMinutesAgo }} min" (`AppSidebar.vue:365-368`, value from `mock/data.ts:23`), "Sem sincronização configurada" (`ShellOverlay.vue:228`), "O resto sincroniza com a conta." (`ShellOverlay.vue:213`) and the "Tema, dados e sync" subtitle (`ShellOverlay.vue:92`). The `SyncStatus` design-system component (`components/ds/SyncStatus.vue`) is not used by the app shell and stays in the gallery; do not add it anywhere. `design/system/README.md` is the design export kept verbatim and is not touched.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `web/src/modules/{library,notes,study,review,projects}/index.ts` and `web/src/shell/` exist; each `index.ts` exports `routes`, `sidebar`, `homeBlocks`, `searchEntries` and `manifest`, and `web/src/views/` no longer exists.
- [ ] With the library manifest set to `backing: 'api'` and `/api/config` returning `modules: []`, a test asserts: the sidebar and the home show no library entry, navigating to `/biblioteca` renders the "módulo desligado" page, and the study, review and projects screens still render.
- [ ] With `/api/config` failing, the app renders "servidor indisponível" and calls the endpoint again; when it starts answering, the app mounts.
- [ ] Sidebar tests cover study+review, study only, review only and neither, and show Revisão nested under Estudo only when both are mounted.
- [ ] A test asserts an `api`-backed library item shows no "link to curriculum" or "make a task" action while study and projects are `mock`-backed.
- [ ] A static import-boundary test proves no file under the study, review or notes modules imports the library's mock slice (the build after the slice is actually deleted is proved by the bead that deletes it).
- [ ] A test renders the shell and the preferences dialog and asserts that none of "Sincronizado há", "Sem sincronização configurada", "sincroniza com a conta", "Tema, dados e sync" appears.
- [ ] `npm run build` and `npm test` pass; every existing behaviour test passes; tests whose only contract is the retired sync copy (for example the sidebar's "Sincronizado há" assertion in `AppShell.test.ts`) are rewritten to assert its absence; every other moved test changes only its imports.
- [ ] Done when: with the library manifest set to `api` and `library` absent from config, the sidebar, the home and the router show no library entry, `/biblioteca` shows the disabled-module page, the mock-backed study, review and projects screens still render, and every existing frontend test passes.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + `@vue/test-utils`, jsdom): mount rule over the four combinations of `backing` and listed/unlisted; disabled-module page; server-unavailable screen with a fake fetch; cross-module action gating.
- Copy (Vitest): the retired-strings test above, over the rendered shell and preferences.
- Regression: the 37 existing test files, moved with their sources.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/` broadly: moves of `views/*`, `mock/*`, `components/AppShell.vue`, `AppSidebar.vue`, `ShellOverlay.vue`, `search/index.ts` and their tests into `modules/<name>/` and `shell/`; `web/src/router/index.ts`; `web/src/main.ts`; new `index.ts` per module; the new disabled-module and server-unavailable pages.
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/client.ts` and `web/src/api/core.d.ts` (the generated config type), `web/src/components/ds/` (not moved).

Frontend only; no file under `server/` is touched. Size L: it moves well over six files of one kind. It cannot be split along a seam that shares no file — the router, `main.ts` and the shell are touched by every part of the move.

title: Add the durable background jobs worker
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing visible yet. This is what lets saving be instant later: slow work (extracting an article's text, asking the classifier where it belongs, replying on Telegram) runs in the background after the save has already returned, retries by itself when a site is briefly down, and survives the server being restarted halfway through. When something fails for good, it shows up as a failed job the person can retry with one command instead of vanishing.

## Outcome
A durable job queue inside `norte serve`: jobs are rows in `core_jobs`, one in-process worker claims them with a lease, renews it while running, retries with a fixed backoff, fails permanently after three attempts or at once on a permanent error, and reclaims jobs whose lease expired after a crash. `norte jobs list` and `norte jobs retry <id>` inspect and requeue them.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app. `server/` is its Go backend: one binary, SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` with one writer connection and a reader pool, goose migrations, sqlc queries. Products are modules switched on by `NORTE_MODULES`; each module registers the job kinds it handles. The "core" (always on, not a module) already has the `core_jobs` table:

`core_jobs(id, kind, payload, dedupe_key, status, attempts, available_at, lease_until, lease_owner, last_error, created_at, started_at, finished_at)`, `status` in `queued|running|done|failed`, index `(status, available_at)`, partial unique index on `dedupe_key` where `status IN ('queued','running')`. Times are fixed-width UTC strings `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ` written through `core.FormatTime`; the clock is `core.Clock`, injectable in tests.

The design, decided:

- **Enqueue.** `core.Jobs.Enqueue(ctx, tx, kind, payload, dedupeKey)` takes the caller's transaction, so a save and its job commit together. `dedupe_key` is nullable; when set and a non-finished job with the same key exists, the call returns that job's id and inserts nothing (enqueueing `extract` for one item twice yields one job).
- **Claim.** One worker goroutine started by `norte serve`. Every 1 s of the injected clock while idle (a "worker cycle"), and again immediately after a job finishes, it claims the oldest `queued` job with `available_at <= now` **whose `kind` has a registered handler** — a job of an unregistered kind (from a module since disabled) stays `queued`, untouched — by setting `status = running`, `lease_until = now + 2 min`, `lease_owner`, `started_at` in the same statement that selects it (`UPDATE ... WHERE id = (SELECT ...) RETURNING ...`) on the single writer, so two claims cannot take one job.
- **Clock and scheduling.** The worker schedules only through the core's `core.Clock` (`Now`, `NewTimer`) and tests use the `core/clocktest` manual clock, both from the database bead. Worker polling, lease renewal, backoff and reclaim use only this clock and never call `time.Sleep`, `time.After` or `time.NewTicker`, so a test can walk minutes of schedule without waiting.
- **Lease renewal.** Every 30 s of the injected clock while the handler runs, the worker extends `lease_until` by two minutes.
- **Attempts are counted at claim.** The claiming statement increments `attempts`, so a job that succeeds on its third run records `attempts = 3`. The handler receives an immutable `core.Job{ID, Kind, Payload, Attempt, MaxAttempts}` (`MaxAttempts = 3`), so a handler can tell its last attempt from an earlier one and perform terminal effects (marking its own row failed, enqueueing a notification) only then.
- **Failure and backoff.** On a handler error (attempts are not incremented again): `last_error` set (redacted: URLs stripped of their query string, never a token), and `available_at = now + 1 min` after the first failure, `+ 5 min` after the second; the third failure sets `failed` and `finished_at`. A handler returning `core.Permanent(err)` (a refused address, a body over a cap, a malformed input) sets `failed` at once with no retry.
- **Reclaim.** At startup and every minute the worker returns `running` jobs whose `lease_until` has passed to `queued`, so a crash mid-job strands nothing. Handlers must therefore be idempotent: a crash after the effect and before the status write replays them. Each handler's bead says what makes it idempotent.
- **In-process on purpose.** A second worker process would be a second deployable for a one-user app and would break "one binary, one container". Heavy runtimes (PDFium later) are created inside the handler and closed when it returns, so their memory is paid only while a job runs.
- **Handler registration.** This bead defines `core.Job{ID, Kind, Payload, Attempt, MaxAttempts}` and `core.JobHandler` (`func(ctx context.Context, job core.Job) error`) in `server/internal/core/jobs.go`, and `core.Jobs.Register(kind, handler)`; the module registry bead, which depends on this one, calls `Register` for each enabled module's `JobHandlers()`. `JobHandlers() map[string]core.JobHandler` on each module (the registry bead mounts them); for this bead, a `core.Jobs.Register(kind, handler)` the registry will call.
- **CLI.** `norte jobs list` (opens the database without migrating; columns id, kind, status, attempts, available_at, last_error) and `norte jobs retry <id>`, which first checks for a `queued` or `running` row with the same non-null `dedupe_key` — if one exists it exits non-zero naming that job and changes neither row, since the partial unique index would otherwise be violated — and otherwise moves the `failed` job back to `queued` with `attempts = 0` and refuses any other status with a non-zero exit.
- **Logging.** Every job logs kind, id, duration and outcome as `slog` JSON; payloads are never logged.
- **Shutdown.** On SIGTERM the worker cancels the handler's context and waits up to the server's 15 s drain. It releases the lease (`status = queued`, `lease_until = NULL`, `attempts = attempts - 1`, so a restart costs no attempt; a reclaim after a crash keeps the count, which bounds a crash loop) only after the handler has returned. If the deadline passes with the handler still running, shutdown logs a non-clean exit and leaves the lease to expire on its own, so the job never becomes claimable while the old handler might still commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With a fake clock, a job whose handler fails twice and succeeds on the third attempt ends `done` with `attempts = 3`, and the test asserts `available_at` was `failure_1 + 1 min` and then `failure_2 + 5 min`.
- [ ] The handler sees `Attempt` = 1, 2, 3 on successive runs and `MaxAttempts` = 3.
- [ ] A handler that fails three times leaves the job `failed` with `attempts = 3`, `finished_at` set and `last_error` holding the last error.
- [ ] A handler returning `core.Permanent(err)` leaves the job `failed` after exactly one attempt.
- [ ] A job set to `running` with `lease_until` in the past (a "dead" worker) is reclaimed by the reclaim pass and then completed by the worker.
- [ ] While a handler blocks for more than 30 s of fake time, `lease_until` is extended at least once and the job is not reclaimed.
- [ ] Two enqueues with the same `dedupe_key` while the first is `queued` yield one row and return the same id; after the first is `done`, a third enqueue with that key inserts a new row.
- [ ] A job of a kind with no registered handler stays `queued` with `attempts = 0` after ten worker cycles.
- [ ] `norte jobs retry <id>` on a `failed` job sets `queued` and `attempts = 0`; on a `done` job it exits non-zero and changes nothing.
- [ ] Advancing the manual clock fires polling, renewal, backoff and reclaim deterministically, and a static test rejects `time.Sleep`, `time.After` and `time.NewTicker` in the worker's source.
- [ ] A handler that ignores cancellation past the drain deadline never has its lease released early, and a second worker cannot claim the job until the lease expires.
- [ ] Retrying a failed job whose `dedupe_key` is held by a queued or running job is refused with a non-zero exit and changes neither row.
- [ ] `(cd server && go test -race ./internal/core -run TestWorkersDoNotDoubleClaim)` passes and `bin/ci` runs it.
- [ ] A job enqueued while the worker is idle is claimed within 1 s of fake time.
- [ ] A job released by a clean shutdown is claimed again with the same `Attempt`; a job reclaimed after a lease expiry is claimed with `Attempt + 1`.
- [ ] `norte jobs list` does not run migrations (a test against a database at an older core version leaves `goose_core` unchanged).
- [ ] Done when: the fake-clock retry, permanent-failure, reclaim, dedupe and unregistered-kind tests above all pass under `go test ./...`.

## Tests
- Unit (Go, `server/internal/core/jobs_test.go`): every criterion above with a fake `core.Clock` and handlers that record their calls; no `time.Sleep` in tests.
- Concurrency (Go unit, run with `-race`): two worker loops against one database claim 50 jobs with no job run twice.
- Integration (Go test invoking the CLI entry point): `jobs list` and `jobs retry` against a temp `NORTE_DATA`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/core/jobs.go` (new), `server/internal/core/jobs_test.go` (new), `server/internal/core/queries/jobs.sql` (new) and its generated `server/internal/core/db/` output, `server/cmd/norte/` (the `jobs` subcommand and starting the worker in `serve`), `bin/ci` (running the claim race test with `-race`).
**Reads only:** `server/internal/core/migrations/` (the `core_jobs` table already exists; this bead adds no migration), the clock and time helpers.

One package, CLI wiring and one gate line: six edited files, so size L.

title: Wire home and search to the API and add the vertical test
description:
## What changes for the user
The home screen and the search box still show invented content. After this lands, Início shows what was really saved — "continuar lendo" from what was opened last and "salvos recentemente" — and the command palette (Ctrl+K) finds a saved item by any word in its text, a subject by name, and the app's screens, all with the keyboard. A single automated test then walks the whole first delivery — save, extract, classify, accept, highlight, question — so it cannot quietly break.

## Outcome
Início's library blocks read the API; `GET /api/core/search` merges each enabled module's search provider plus subjects; the command palette merges it with the static screen index in an accessible combobox; the Estudo home's dead search box is wired or removed. A Go end-to-end test proves the loop and runs in `bin/ci`.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. Its first delivery is "read": save a link, have it reappear at the right moment, read it, and end the reading in something that survives the day. `server/` is the Go backend; the library (items, full-text search over title, author, why, headings and text with `bm25` weights, extraction and classification jobs), notes (highlights, annotations, questions) and the core (subjects, links, focus, a stub LLM server for tests) are in place. Each module implements `SearchEntries(ctx, q, limit)` returning `core.SearchEntry{id, module, type, title, subtitle, path}` where `path` is the frontend route that opens it (`/biblioteca/<id>` for a library item, `/assuntos/<slug>` for a subject); the library's provider is its FTS query. The extraction job refuses loopback and private addresses on purpose (SSRF protection), so a test cannot make the server fetch an `httptest` page — it must send the page as an HTML snapshot, the way the browser extension does.

`web/` is the Vue 3 frontend. The command palette lives in `ShellOverlay` (mode `busca`; opened by ⌘K/Ctrl+K in `AppShell`), indexed by `web/src/search/index.ts` (`createSearchIndex`, `filterSearchIndex`, `groupSearchResults`) — now under `web/src/shell/`. The Início view has mock blocks and a `#home-search` box bound to a value nothing uses; the Estudo home has a `#study-search` input with no binding at all. Library items carry `last_opened_at` and `saved_at`.

Decided:

title: Add subjects, focus, links and the subject page
description:
## What changes for the user
A saved link finally has somewhere to go. After this lands, the person can create subjects ("Kubernetes", "Escrita"), link a link to one when saving or later, and open a subject's page to see everything saved about it, counted by kind. A subject can be marked as a current focus with one switch. Subjects get their own entry in the sidebar, and the subjects on the Estudo home open their page instead of the whole library.

## Outcome
The core's subjects API (CRUD, focus toggle, lookup by slug, per-kind counts), `GET /api/core/focus`, the links API (create manual, list by end, decide a suggestion), and the frontend: the subject screen `/assuntos/:slug`, a reusable "Salvos sobre isso" panel, a link picker in the save dialog and on an item, the Estudo home's subjects linking to their pages, "novo assunto" controls, a top-level "Assuntos" sidebar section, and the "Listas" group hidden while study is mock-backed.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. Its core problem, measured on the person: a link saved is almost always the right thing found at the wrong moment — a subject of real interest that is not the current focus — and nothing brings it back when the subject becomes the focus. Subjects and links are how a saved item gets a destination.

`server/` is the Go backend; the always-on "core" (not a module) already has the tables `core_subjects(id, name, slug UNIQUE, focus, created_at)`, `core_subject_aliases(alias_slug, subject_id)`, the item registry `core_items(id, module, type, title, url)` and `core_links(id, src_id, dst_id, kind, source, status, confidence, created_at, decided_at)` with `UNIQUE(src_id, dst_id, kind)`, `kind` in `about|material_of|derived_from|blocks`, `source` in `manual|llm`, `status` in `confirmed|suggested|rejected`. `core_links` is the only relation between modules. A subject is registered in `core_items` like any other link target. The core's contract is `api/openapi/core.yaml`, routes under `/api/core/`. Each module may implement `FocusTargets(ctx)` (title, id, type of what it considers "in progress"); the library implements none; study and projects (later deliveries) will. The library already saves items with an optional `link_to` list that creates `about` links.

`web/` is the Vue 3 frontend, organised by module, with the library and notes reading the API. The sidebar is `AppSidebar` (now under `web/src/shell/`): today the Estudo group has an "Assuntos" child (route `estudo` with hash `#assuntos`, a count summed from module counts, commented as "no subject entity"), and the Biblioteca children end with a "Listas" sub-heading listing library items by curriculum. The Estudo home (`StudyHomeView`, a mock-backed study screen) has a subjects grid (heading `#study-subjects`) whose every entry links to `/biblioteca?v=tudo`.

Decided:

- **Subjects API**: `GET /api/core/subjects?q=&cursor=&limit=` and `POST /api/core/subjects`, where `q` matches accent-insensitively over the normalised name and the aliases (exact, then prefix, then substring, ties by slug then id) and returns each canonical subject once, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/core/subjects/{id}` (`PATCH` renames and toggles `focus`; the slug is derived from the name — lowercase, accents stripped, punctuation removed, spaces to hyphens — and a collision is 409), `GET /api/core/subjects/by-slug/{slug}`. `GET /api/core/subjects/{id}` returns per-kind counts of the library items linked to it (`confirmed` links only). Creating or renaming a subject registers or updates its `core_items` row. Deleting a subject runs, in one writer transaction, the delete and `core.UnregisterItem` for its registry row; the registry row's cascade removes every link to and from it, and the alias cascade removes its aliases. Subjects are created from the UI or the CLI (`norte subjects add|list|focus <name>`), never by an LLM on its own.
- **Focus**: `GET /api/core/focus` returns the subjects with `focus = true` plus every enabled module's `FocusTargets` (the registry injects the enabled modules into the core focus service as `[]core.FocusProvider`; the core never imports the registry), each `{id, type, title}`. "In progress" is defined by each module. Focus is derived, not declared; the subject `focus` flag is the smallest version of an explicit focus, and it is what makes "what to read now" and the classifier testable before curricula and projects exist.
- **Links API**: `POST /api/core/links` (calls `core.Links.Confirm`; an end not in `core_items` is 400; manual, created `confirmed`; on an existing `suggested` or `rejected` pair for the same `(src, dst, kind)` it flips that row to `confirmed` with `source = manual` and `decided_at` set, rather than failing on the unique index), `GET /api/core/links?dst_id=&src_id=&status=&cursor=&limit=` (every filter optional; `status` alone lists the suggestion queue, ordered by `created_at` descending then id and served by a new core index on `(status, created_at)`; each item is `{id, kind, source, status, confidence, created_at, decided_at, src: {id, module, type, title, url}, dst: {...}}` with both ends read from `core_items`), `POST /api/core/links/{id}/decide` (`accept` → `confirmed`, `reject` → `rejected`, setting `decided_at`). A rejected row stays as the record that the pair was rejected.
- **Lists** (subjects, links) are cursor-paginated like every list in Norte: `cursor` and `limit` (default 50), a documented total order with the id as tie-breaker, the filters hashed into the cursor (a cursor reused with other filters is refused with 400), and a `{items, next_cursor}` envelope; the sidebar, the picker, the panel and the suggestion queue load all pages or offer "carregar mais".
- **Deleting a subject** from its screen: the delete action first fetches the number of links to and from it, names that count in a confirmation dialog, and calls `DELETE` only after explicit confirmation; cancelling sends nothing.
- **Subject screen** `/assuntos/:slug`: name, focus switch, per-kind counts, and the "Salvos sobre isso" panel. Counts and lists come only from enabled, `api`-backed modules.
- **"Salvos sobre isso"**: a panel component listing the library items linked (`confirmed`, `about`) to a given target id. Placed on the subject page now; built to be reused by the curriculum and project pages in later deliveries, so it takes the target id as its only input.
- **Link picker** in the Início save dialog and on an item: fed by `GET /api/core/focus` first, then a subject search; selecting creates the link (on save via `link_to`, on an item via `POST /api/core/links`).
- **Sidebar**: a top-level "Assuntos" section listing subjects (links to `/assuntos/:slug`); the old "Assuntos" child under Estudo is removed, since the top-level entry replaces it. The "Listas" group is hidden while `study` is mock-backed — an `api` library item cannot point at mock curricula — and returns in the study delivery fed by `material_of` links.
- **Estudo home**: the subjects grid lists real subjects and each opens its subject page; a "novo assunto" control on the grid and on the subject page.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `POST /api/core/subjects {name: "Machine Learning"}` returns slug `machine-learning` and a `core_items` row of type `subject`; a second subject with the same name returns 409.
- [ ] An item linked to a subject (on save via `link_to`, or later via `POST /api/core/links`) appears on `/assuntos/<slug>` with the right per-kind count, and the subject appears in the sidebar's Assuntos section.
- [ ] Toggling focus on a subject adds it to and removes it from `GET /api/core/focus`.
- [ ] Deleting a subject removes its subject, alias, registry and link rows; the dialog names the link count; cancelling sends no request.
- [ ] Subject search finds a subject by its name typed without accents and by an alias, returns it once, in a stable order.
- [ ] 120 subjects page as 50/50/20; a links cursor reused with changed filters is refused with 400.
- [ ] `POST /api/core/links` on a pair previously `rejected`, and on a pair currently `suggested`, sets it to `confirmed` and leaves one row; `decide reject` on a `suggested` link sets `rejected` and `decided_at`.
- [ ] The "Salvos sobre isso" panel, given a target id, lists exactly the `confirmed` `about` links to it (a suggested or rejected link is not listed).
- [ ] The Estudo home's subjects open `/assuntos/:slug`; the old Estudo "Assuntos" child is gone; the "Listas" group is not rendered while study is mock-backed.
- [ ] `norte subjects add "Escrita"`, `norte subjects list` and `norte subjects focus "Escrita"` work against a temp `NORTE_DATA`.
- [ ] Done when: an item linked to a subject appears on that subject's page with the right per-kind count and in the sidebar's Assuntos section, and toggling focus on a subject changes `/api/core/focus`.

## Tests
- Unit (Go): slug derivation over a table (accents, punctuation, case).
- Integration (Go, `httptest` + temp `NORTE_DATA`): subjects CRUD and counts; focus; links create/flip/decide; CLI.
- Component (Vitest, fake providers): subject screen, panel, link picker, sidebar section, Listas hidden under a mock-backed study.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `api/openapi/core.yaml` (subjects, focus, links) and its generated outputs, `server/internal/core/` (a migration adding the `(status, created_at)` index on `core_links`, subjects, focus, links services and handlers, `subjects` CLI), `web/src/shell/` (sidebar, subject screen, link picker, the panel component), `web/src/modules/study/` (the Estudo home subjects grid only), `web/src/modules/library/` (link picker on an item), `server/internal/app/` (injecting `[]core.FocusProvider`), `server/cmd/norte/` (mounting the `subjects` CLI), the frontend router (the `/assuntos/:slug` route).
**Reads only:** `core_subjects`/`core_links` schema (already migrated).

Server core and three frontend areas; size L.

## Recovery path
No migration: the subject and link tables already exist. The one destructive operation added is deleting a subject, which cascades to its links and its registry row; the UI asks for confirmation and names the number of linked items before deleting. A wrongly deleted subject is recreated by hand and its items relinked; there is no undo in this version.

title: Port the base design-system components to Vue
description:
## What changes for the user
Screens cannot be built until the buttons, tabs, titles and panels they share exist. After this lands, every screen can use the same controls the prototype shows, in both themes.

## Outcome
Vue SFCs in `web/src/components/ds/` for Button, Tag, SyncStatus, Stat, ProgressBar, StreakGrid, PageTitle, NavItem, SectionHeader, SegmentedControl, Tabs, SidePanel, TextField and Icon. Each matches its README, its props in `index.d.ts` and its screenshot.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

The Icon names are check, play, plus, lock, arrow, arrowLeft, chevronDown, collapse, expand, external, note, comment and image.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All 14 components exist in `web/src/components/ds/` with props typed as in `index.d.ts`.
- [ ] SegmentedControl, Tabs and TextField support `v-model`; SidePanel supports `v-model:collapsed`.
- [ ] Styling uses only token CSS variables; no hex colour literal appears in these files.
- [ ] A dev-only route `/_ds` renders every component in each of its documented variants, and in both themes it matches the screenshots by eye.
- [ ] Done when: `/_ds` shows all 14 components matching their screenshots, and the gate is green.

## Tests
- Component: one test per component covering its props and emitted events (for example, SegmentedControl emits `update:modelValue` on click, and Button renders each variant class).

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/components/ds/`, `web/src/views/DsGallery.vue`, `web/src/router/index.ts`

The gallery route is the only router change.

title: Build the server skeleton, the build pipeline and the gate
description:
## What changes for the user
Today Norte only runs as a development server over mock data, and there is no single thing to install. After this lands, one command builds one program, `norte`, and running `norte serve` opens the current app in the browser from that program alone. Nothing the person sees in the app changes yet; what changes is that Norte becomes something that can be installed, started and kept running, and that every later change is checked by the same gate on every machine.

## Outcome
A Go module under `server/` builds the `norte` binary: a cobra CLI with `serve`, `migrate`, `version` and `config`; a config loader; `slog` JSON logging with a request id; an HTTP server with timeouts, a body cap, a `Host` allowlist, a content security policy and graceful shutdown; a plain `GET /api/health`; the built frontend embedded and served with history fallback. `bin/generate` builds the frontend and copies it into the embed directory atomically, the Vite dev server proxies `/api` to the binary, `bin/ci` is the one gate, a GitHub Actions workflow runs it, and `AGENTS.md` describes the monorepo as it now is.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI, used from a desktop browser and a phone. Today the application is only `web/` (Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript, Vue Router, Vitest under jsdom; scripts `dev`, `build` = `vue-tsc --build --force && vite build`, `test` = `vitest run`), plus design assets under `design/` and the tracker in `.beads/` (git-ignored planning notes under `docs/` and `local/` may exist locally and are not part of the build). There is no `server/`, no `bin/`, no `.github/`, no `Dockerfile`, no Node version pin. Everything runs on mock data. The current gate, stated in `AGENTS.md`, is `npm run build && npm test` in `web/`.

The backend decided for it: Go, one static binary, no CGO; SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite`; `sqlc` and `goose` (later beads); an OpenAPI contract per module (later bead); no authentication in v1 — the server listens on localhost or the Tailscale network. The binary embeds the built frontend and serves UI and API together. This bead is the skeleton every other backend bead builds on, and its gate is the gate they all run under — which is why it goes first.

What it contains, decided:

- **Layout.** `server/go.mod` (Go 1.26 via the `toolchain` directive; Go tools pinned as tool dependencies), `server/cmd/norte/main.go`, `server/internal/app/` (config, server wiring), `server/internal/core/` (logging, HTTP helpers), `server/internal/webassets/` (the embed). Every `go` command runs from `server/`; `bin/ci` and `bin/generate` `cd` there.
- **CLI (cobra).** `norte serve` starts the HTTP server; `norte migrate` exists as a command (it applies nothing until the database bead); `norte version` prints the version; `norte config` prints the effective configuration and the source of each value (flag, env, file, default), with secrets redacted. `config` and `version` never open a database.
- **Config.** Every setting is accepted as `NORTE_<NAME>` and in an optional TOML file at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/norte/config.toml` (or `--config <path>`); non-secret settings also as a flag; precedence flag over env over file over default. Secrets (`NORTE_LLM_KEY`, `NORTE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`) are never flags, because a flag is visible to every process through the process list. A config file holding a secret that is readable by group or others makes `serve` print a warning naming the file. The loader expands `~` itself (Go does not). Settings and defaults: `NORTE_DATA` (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/norte` or `~/.local/share/norte`), `NORTE_MODULES` (every compiled module), `NORTE_LISTEN` (`127.0.0.1:8080`), `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL` (empty), `NORTE_TIMEZONE` (system zone), `NORTE_LLM_URL`, `NORTE_LLM_MODEL`, `NORTE_LLM_KEY` (empty), `NORTE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`, `NORTE_TELEGRAM_CHAT` (empty), `NORTE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES` (`20971520`), `NORTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (`67108864`), `NORTE_LOG_LEVEL` (`info`). The loader knows them all now so later beads only read them.
- **Logging.** `log/slog` JSON on stderr. Every request logs method, path, status, duration and request id. Request bodies, HTML payloads and tokens are never logged; URLs are logged with the query string stripped.
- **HTTP.** `net/http` with the Go 1.22 pattern router, no framework (a framework would be a second way to do what `net/http` does). Middleware: request id (`X-Request-Id`, generated when absent, echoed in every error body); `Host` allowlist (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, the host of `NORTE_LISTEN`, the host of `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL`; anything else gets 421 — with no authentication, a DNS-rebinding page in the browser could otherwise read the server); panic recovery; body cap `NORTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (413 above it); JSON error shape `{"error": {"code", "message", "field"?, "request_id"}}`. Server timeouts: read header 10 s, read 60 s, write 60 s, idle 120 s. Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM: stop accepting, drain in-flight requests up to 15 s, close.
- **Content security policy**, sent on every response: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' https: data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. Inline styles are allowed because the design system and extracted articles use them (tightening was considered and deferred); scripts get no exception. So the inline theme-bootstrap script in `web/index.html` (lines 8-15: it sets `<html data-theme>` from `localStorage['norte-theme']`, falling back to light) moves to `web/public/theme-bootstrap.js`, loaded from `<head>` with a classic `<script src="/theme-bootstrap.js">` (not `type="module"`, which Vite would defer past first paint, bringing back the theme flash the inline script exists to prevent),, keeping its behaviour, so the served frontend works under the policy from day one.
- **Health.** A plain hand-written `GET /api/health` returning 200 and a small JSON body. The contract bead later replaces it with a generated handler.
- **Embedding.** Go's `embed` cannot reach outside the package directory, so `bin/generate` copies the built frontend into `server/internal/webassets/dist/`. Directive `//go:embed all:dist`. `.gitignore` gets `server/internal/webassets/dist/*` with `!server/internal/webassets/dist/placeholder.html`, so a committed placeholder keeps the package compiling before the first build. The handler serves files from the embed and falls back to `index.html` for any non-`/api/` path that is not a file (Vue Router uses HTML5 history), and returns 404 JSON for unknown `/api/` paths.
- **`bin/generate`.** For now: `npm ci` if needed, `npm run build` in `web/`, then an atomic swap: build into `dist.new` (copying the placeholder into it), rename `dist` to `dist.old`, rename `dist.new` to `dist`, remove `dist.old`. A failed build never leaves a half-written directory. The contract bead later adds the generators in front.
- **Vite proxy.** `web/vite.config.ts` has no `server` block today (it is 14 lines: the Vue plugin and the `@` alias). Add `server.proxy['/api']` to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` so `npm run dev` talks to a locally running `norte serve`.
- **`bin/ci`.** The one gate, and exactly what CI runs: `gofmt -l` failing on any output, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` with a temporary `NORTE_DATA`, `bin/generate`, `npm run build` and `npm test` in `web/`. Before building it compares the Go version in `server/go.mod`'s `toolchain` directive with the one in the workflow (and, once it exists, the Dockerfile), and `web/.node-version` with the workflow's Node setup, failing with both files and versions on a mismatch. Later beads add their checks to it.
- **GitHub workflow.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `bin/ci` on push and pull request, with the Go version repeated from the `toolchain` directive and Node pinned (add a `.node-version` in `web/` and use it from the workflow).
- **`AGENTS.md`.** Rewrite it to describe the monorepo as it now is: `web/` and `server/`; one OpenAPI file per module under `api/openapi/` (not a single `openapi.yaml`, which is what it says today); generated code under `server/gen/api/`, `server/internal/*/db/` and `web/src/api/` is never edited; `bin/ci` is the gate (replacing `npm run build && npm test`); every `go` command runs from `server/`. Preserve every existing rule that is still true — the design-system location under `design/system/` with its tokens, components and fonts, the git-ignored prototype workflow under `design/prototypes/`, the public-repo rule (neutral invented mock content only), UI strings in Portuguese with code, comments and commits in English, work tracked in `br` — and replace only what this bead makes false: the backend's absence, the single `openapi.yaml`, and the old gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)` produces one binary at `server/norte`; `(cd server && ./norte serve)` on a free port serves the current frontend at `/`, and a deep link such as `/biblioteca` returns the app's `index.html` (history fallback).
- [ ] `GET /api/health` returns 200; `GET /api/nope` returns 404 with the JSON error shape and a `request_id`.
- [ ] A request with `Host: evil.example` gets 421; `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, the host of `NORTE_LISTEN` and the host of `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL` (each with the port) succeed.
- [ ] A middleware unit test mounts a test-only handler that reads its body and proves that a body over `NORTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES`, sent both with `Content-Length` and chunked, gets 413 with the JSON error shape (no public route reads a body yet).
- [ ] A captured access-log line has method, path without its query string, status, duration and request id, and contains neither the request body nor a token passed in the query.
- [ ] Every response carries the `Content-Security-Policy` header with the exact policy in Context, and `web/index.html` contains no inline `<script>` body; switching theme to dark and reloading still opens dark.
- [ ] `norte config` prints each setting with its source; with `NORTE_LLM_KEY=secret` set, the output contains no `secret`; no flag named `--llm-key` or `--telegram-token` exists.
- [ ] A config file containing `llm_key` with mode `0644` makes `serve` log a warning naming the file; with mode `0600` it does not.
- [ ] `NORTE_DATA=~/x norte config` shows the expanded home path.
- [ ] SIGTERM during a slow request lets it complete (up to 15 s) and the process exits 0.
- [ ] With `norte serve` running, `npm run dev` in `web/` answers `/api/health` through the proxy.
- [ ] `bin/ci` exits 0 on a fresh clone, and the GitHub workflow runs it green on the PR.
- [ ] A workflow fixture with a mismatched Go or Node version makes the pin check fail naming both values.
- [ ] After the rewrite, `AGENTS.md` still names `design/system/` (tokens, components, fonts) and the git-ignored prototype workflow.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` names `bin/ci` as the gate and `api/openapi/<module>.yaml` as the contract layout, and no longer mentions a single `openapi.yaml`.
- [ ] Done when: `norte serve` serves the current frontend from one binary built by `bin/generate && go build`, `npm run dev` reaches it through the proxy, and `bin/ci` is green on a clean clone.

## Tests
- Unit (Go): config precedence (flag over env over file over default), `~` expansion, secret redaction in `config` output, permission warning; `Host` allowlist; body cap (test-only body-reading handler, `Content-Length` and chunked); access-log fields and redaction; error shape; CSP header present; history fallback versus `/api/` 404.
- Integration (Go, `httptest` against the real handler with a placeholder `dist`): health, fallback.
- Subprocess integration (Go test that builds and starts the binary): block an in-flight request, send SIGTERM, release it, assert the request completes and the process exits 0.
- Frontend (Vitest, existing suite): still green after the theme script moves; one test asserts the theme module applies the stored theme.
- Gate: the workflow run on the PR is the proof that `bin/ci` is green outside the author's machine.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/` (new: `go.mod`, `cmd/norte/main.go`, `internal/app/`, `internal/core/` logging and HTTP helpers, `internal/webassets/` with `dist/placeholder.html`), `bin/generate` (new), `bin/ci` (new), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new), `.gitignore`, `web/index.html`, `web/public/theme-bootstrap.js` (new), `web/vite.config.ts`, `web/.node-version` (new), `AGENTS.md`.
**Reads only:** `web/src/theme.ts` (the storage key `norte-theme`), `web/package.json`.

Spans the new server module, the frontend's entry and build config, the gate scripts and the CI workflow. Size L. It is not split because its parts share the gate: the skeleton is only "done" when `bin/ci` and the workflow prove it, and the workflow has nothing to run without the skeleton.

Reviewer fixed the timezone default and a non-hermetic config test (rework:2).
